certificate.mechanical_relation: XOR of all four component-incidence rows is zero, the exact-rank affine offset occurs four times and cancels, but XOR of outcome codes is 1.

findings.statement: The 5x3-k3 exact-rank affine-XOR failure has an explicit four-state same-rank dependency certificate. All component coefficients and the rank-9 affine offset cancel, while the relative outcome code XOR is nonzero.

The substitution T09415 <-> T09407 is value-neutral in context T07229 (win -> win) but value-changing in context T07351 + T09436 (draw -> loss). Therefore no context-independent additive value can be assigned to that substitution under the tested GF(2)^2 model.

Because exact rank + component parity + T2 remains Q-V sufficient on 5x3-k3, this certificate is not a representation collision. It localizes the obstruction to D_G: the scalar map on the frozen quotient is nonlinear/contextual with respect to independent component XOR coordinates.

The four-row contradiction is invariant under any injective recoding of loss/draw/win into GF(2)^2. Every such recoding differs by an affine permutation of the four-point GF(2)^2 space; four affine offsets cancel and the invertible linear part preserves a nonzero certificate syndrome.

Independent component valuation is therefore falsified in this carrier even with exact-rank grading. The evidence supports at least one contextual interaction term or a non-additive finite decoder, but does not yet establish that pairwise interactions are sufficient.

Before fitting pairwise terms globally, classify the twelve size-4 certificates to determine whether they are generated by one repeated contextual substitution motif or by multiple independent nonlinear motifs.

nonclaims: This does not falsify the bounded Q-V sufficiency of component parity + rank phase + T2.
This does not prove a pairwise polynomial evaluator.
This does not falsify all XOR-like finite algebras.
next_question: Do the twelve 5x3-k3 four-state rectangles share one structural substitution/context motif, or do they require multiple independent interaction generators?
